lines.en: It is often a simple frustration that leads to the most useful inventions.
The smartphone is said to have changed our lives more than any invention of the last fifty years.
What the inventor never expected was that her creation would be used in hospitals around the world.
Not only did the printing press spread knowledge, but it also changed who was allowed to have it.
However advanced an invention may be, it is useless unless people can actually afford it.
Were electricity to be invented today, it would surely be called impossible by the experts of the age.
It is not the strongest idea that survives, but the one that adapts fastest to change.
Little by little, the invention moved from a luxury of the rich to a necessity for everyone.
What drives most inventors is not money, but the joy of solving a problem nobody else could solve.
Rarely does a single person invent anything great alone; every breakthrough stands on earlier work.
What no one predicted was that the most successful product of the decade would be a device nobody asked for.
It is not enough for an invention to work; it must also fit into people's daily habits.
So rapidly is artificial intelligence developing that even its creators admit they cannot predict its limits.
Were the patent to expire tomorrow, dozens of companies would copy the design within a month.
It was a failed experiment, of all things, that gave the world one of its most important medicines.
